title: Chinese expert debates on EU-China economic frictions + Gotion-PowerCo deal + Electric car exports
gist: MERICS Europe-China 360 brief (Grzegorz Stec) reports that Chinese experts now accept EU-China economic frictions as enduring but expect trade interdependence, retaliation risk and EU member-state divisions to restrain Brussels into 'competitive coexistence'. Meanwhile the EU is pairing de-escalation with assertive tools, including a planned DiversifyEU instrument, a Solidarity Mechanism and a conceptual market-access 'kill-switch'.

themes.theme: Chinese expert views on EU frictions

insights.claim: Chinese think-tank and academic experts now see economic frictions as an enduring feature of EU-China relations, a shift from spring 2026 when many dismissed EU overproduction concerns.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Beijing is preparing for prolonged trade friction with Europe rather than a reset.

insights.claim: Chinese experts' acceptance of competition does not mean they agree with Europe's diagnosis that unfair Chinese competition practices cause trade imbalances.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: No concession on the core overcapacity dispute is likely from Beijing.

insights.claim: Several Chinese experts expect trade interdependence, retaliation risk and divisions among EU member states to constrain Brussels and let relations settle into competitive coexistence.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Beijing is betting EU trade defence will be diluted; investors should watch member-state unity as the swing factor.
insights.locator: The expert comments came in the context

insights.claim: Yu Xiang of CASS's Institute of American Studies argues China-US-Europe competition will shift from commodity trade to institutional power, including rule-setting for green and AI transitions.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Standards and subsidy rules for green tech and AI become the next battleground.
insights.quote: the focus of tripartite competition will shift from commodity trade to institutional power

insights.claim: Chinese experts project confidence that Beijing could withstand a trade war with Europe, citing its perceived success in standing firm against the Trump administration and securing US acceptance of 'strategic stability'.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Beijing's perceived win vs Washington emboldens it versus Brussels, raising escalation risk.
insights.locator: A broader group of Chinese experts

insights.claim: The 8-9 October 2026 EU-China Trade and Investment Consultations produced an 'understanding' on curbing exports of Chinese-made hybrid vehicles to Europe.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Chinese hybrid exports to Europe may be capped, shifting competitive dynamics for EU automakers.
insights.locator: The expert comments came in the context

insights.claim: After the consultations, the European Council called for broader use of trade defense instruments, and the Commission said it would propose a DiversifyEU instrument and a Solidarity Mechanism in December.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: December 2026 is a catalyst date for new EU economic-security tools.
insights.locator: In the week after the consultations

insights.claim: Building on a Franco-German paper of October 5, the Commission will conceptualise a 'kill-switch' instrument to quickly disrupt China's and others' access to the single market.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: A market-access kill-switch would materially raise tail risk for Chinese firms selling into the EU.
insights.locator: In the week after the consultations

insights.claim: The EU is running a dual-track approach, pairing efforts to defuse trade tensions with intensified preparation of assertive tools.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Expect simultaneous deal-making and escalation capacity-building from Brussels.
insights.locator: In the week after the consultations

insights.claim: VW's PowerCo and China's Gotion High Tech are moving ahead on a joint venture before the EU has set rules for such deals.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Chinese battery JVs in Europe face regulatory uncertainty from forthcoming EU rules.

insights.claim: The EU's share of China's fully electric car exports has stayed steady in 2026 despite EU tariffs.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: EU EV tariffs have not displaced Chinese EV exports to Europe so far.
